# kopia_repository_description (Resource)

Manages the description of the Kopia server's repository connection: the name the Kopia UI shows for the repository, which Kopia sets to `Repository in <storage>` — such as `Repository in Filesystem: /repository` — until it is changed.

This is a singleton: a Kopia server has one description, so declare at most one of these resources. Kopia saves the description in the server's config file, `repository.config`, not in the repository, so other clients of the same repository keep their own; the `kopia_repository_status` data source reports it as `description`. Disconnecting the repository deletes the config file, and with it the description.

~> **Destroying this resource leaves the description in place.** Kopia's API can set a description but not remove one, so destroying only removes the resource from Terraform state.

~> **Kopia rewrites its whole config file with the settings the server started with whenever the description changes.** That would put the saved throttle limits back to those the server started with, so after each change the provider saves the limits in effect again, without changing them, under the same lock `kopia_throttle` takes; when that fails, the apply fails, and the next apply sets the description and saves the limits again. Other changes made to the file since the server started, with `kopia repository set-client` or `kopia cache set`, are reverted all the same.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The description the Kopia UI shows for the repository. This is a singleton,
# so declare at most one. Kopia saves it in the server's config file, not in
# the repository, and destroying this resource leaves it in place.
resource "kopia_repository_description" "this" {
  description = "Production backups (managed by Terraform)"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `description` (String) Description of the repository. It must not be empty: Kopia saves `""` as no description at all, and puts its default back at the next restart.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Always `description`: a Kopia server has one repository description.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# There is only one repository description, so the import id is always
# "description". Read then fills in the description the server reports.
terraform import kopia_repository_description.this description
```
